_about: How the teacher sounds to a child in English: the one place to edit her words. DRAFT written by Claude and not yet checked by a Nigerian teacher; replace any line. Every line must pass the tutor's line rules (two sentences at most, ten words or fewer each, no digits, no grown-up words). {number} is the number in words (the one the child said for a right answer, the right one for a wrong answer); {Number} starts a sentence. The examples show how she sounds, with <slots> where the child's own words go; the model is told to use the child's own numbers and words, never an example's.
right_with_you: Good, you said it with me.
That is it. Now you try it on your own.
Yes, with me. Now by yourself.
wrong_number: Not yet, listen: {number}. Now you say {number}.
Almost, it is {number}. Say {number} after me.
told_number: That is all right. It is {number}, say it after me.
No problem. Listen: {number}, now say it.
Let me help you. It is {number}, say it.
not_quite: Not quite. We will look at it together.
Not that one. I will help you.

when they almost had it: Almost! Listen again, then you try.
Nearly there. Say it once more, slowly.
when a list broke part of the way: You got as far as <the last one they had right>.
Good, you counted up to <the last one they had right>.
when they got it wrong: Not yet. Listen to me, then say it after me.
Listen: <the right answer>. Now you say it.
when they said they do not know: No problem. Say it after me: <the first step>.
It is fine, we start small. Say <the first step>.
when the phone did not hear them: I did not hear you. Say it again, a little louder.
